doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Duo Paloma with his wife and refusing restrictions
summary: His wife, a classical concert pianist, now plays jazz and they perform as Duo Paloma; he stresses playing African, Chinese and Indian music without restriction.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And then I had, now my wife is a concert pianist from the Polish National Conservatory but she did her doctorate here in piano at Florida State and then a couple of years ago she decided she was going to be jazz. So she spends hours every day, hours with an S, every day, I mean like every, like seven days a week you know learning jazz tunes and just working on this with that great classical technique that she has. So we call ourselves Duo Paloma. And we were just a strictly classical duo playing the French trumpet piano literature that’s so interesting and that kind of stuff and adapting other literature to trumpet and piano. But now we have the improvisational element added to it. So I’ve always wanted to play with a pianist who understood something about classical composition. So this gives me that.
Yeah, that’s a rare combination, to have someone who can live in both worlds like that.

Yeah, I insist on not being restricted. You know I’ve had a good time playing with Africans, playing African music. We have one recording we did with a company that we think is the first instance of the Chinese guzheng and the Indian sitar playing Indian classical music together.
